sanskrit: tataḥ karṇo mahārāja preṣayām āsa sāyakān suvarṇapuṅkhāñ śatrughnān khacarān rākṣasān prati
english: Then, great king, Karṇa loosed his arrows—gold-feathered, foe-slaying—against the sky-roving rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tad bāṇair arditaṃ yūthaṃ rakṣasāṃ pīnavakṣasām siṃhenevārditaṃ vanyaṃ gajānām ākulaṃ kulam
english: That host of broad-chested demons, tormented by his shafts, was thrown into confusion like a wild herd of elephants harried by a lion.

sanskrit: vidhamya rākṣasān bāṇaiḥ sāśvasūtagajān vibhuḥ dadāha bhagavān vahnir bhūtānīva yugakṣaye
english: Scattering the rākṣasas with his arrows, together with their horses, charioteers, and elephants, the mighty lord consumed them as the blessed fire devours all beings at the ending of an age.

sanskrit: sa hatvā rākṣasīṃ senāṃ śuśubhe sūtanandanaḥ pureva tripuraṃ dagdhvā divi devo maheśvaraḥ
english: Having slain the host of rākṣasas, the son of the charioteer shone forth like the god Maheśvara of old in heaven, when he had burned the three cities to ash.

sanskrit: teṣu rājasahasreṣu pāṇḍaveyeṣu māriṣa nainaṃ nirīkṣitum api kaś cic chaknoti pārthiva
english: Among those thousands of kings on the Pāṇḍava side, good sir, not one, O lord of the earth, was able even to look upon him.

sanskrit: ṛte ghaṭotkacād rājan rākṣasendrān mahābalāt bhīmavīryabalopetāt kruddhād vaivasvatād iva
english: None save Ghaṭotkaca, O king—that mighty lord of the rākṣasas, endowed with terrible valor and strength, and now enraged like the son of Vivasvat himself.

sanskrit: tasya kruddhasya netrābhyāṃ pāvakaḥ samajāyata maholkābhyāṃ yathā rājan sārciṣaḥ snehabindavaḥ
english: From the eyes of that enraged one fire was born, O king, as flaming drops of oil fall blazing from two great meteors.

sanskrit: talaṃ talena saṃhatya saṃdaśya daśanacchadam ratham āsthāya ca punar māyayā nirmitaṃ punaḥ
english: Smiting palm against palm and biting his lip, he mounted once more a chariot newly fashioned by his magic.

sanskrit: yuktaṃ gajanibhair vāhaiḥ piśācavadanaiḥ kharaiḥ sa sūtam abravīt kruddhaḥ sūtaputrāya mā vaha
english: It was yoked with mounts like elephants—asses with the faces of fiends—and in his wrath he said to his driver: "Bear me against the son of the charioteer."

sanskrit: sa yayau ghorarūpeṇa rathena rathināṃ varaḥ dvairathaṃ sūtaputreṇa punar eva viśāṃ pate
english: And so, O lord of peoples, that foremost of chariot-warriors went forth again in his fearsome car to a duel with the son of the charioteer.

sanskrit: sa cikṣepa punaḥ kruddhaḥ sūtaputrāya rākṣasaḥ aṣṭacakrāṃ mahāghorām aśaniṃ rudranirmitām
english: Once more in his fury the rākṣasa hurled at the son of the charioteer a most terrible eight-wheeled thunderbolt, fashioned by Rudra.

sanskrit: tām avaplutya jagrāha karṇo nyasya rathe dhanuḥ cikṣepa caināṃ tasyaiva syandanāt so 'vapupluve
english: Leaping up, Karṇa caught it, laying his bow aside in the chariot, and flung it back at him; whereupon the rākṣasa sprang down from his car.

sanskrit: sāśvasūtadhvajaṃ yānaṃ bhasma kṛtvā mahāprabhā viveśa vasudhāṃ bhittvā surās tatra visismiyuḥ
english: That weapon of great brilliance reduced the chariot, with its horses, driver, and banner, to ashes, then cleft the earth and entered it; and the gods marveled at the sight.

sanskrit: karṇaṃ tu sarvabhūtāni pūjayām āsur añjasā yad avaplutya jagrāha devasṛṣṭāṃ mahāśanim
english: All beings straightway honored Karṇa, in that he had leaped up and seized the great god-fashioned thunderbolt.

sanskrit: evaṃ kṛtvā raṇe karṇa āruroha rathaṃ punaḥ tato mumoca nārācān sūtaputraḥ paraṃtapaḥ
english: Having done this in battle, Karṇa mounted his chariot again, and then the son of the charioteer, scorcher of foes, let fly his iron shafts.

sanskrit: aśakyaṃ kartum anyena sarvabhūteṣu mānada yad akārṣīt tadā karṇaḥ saṃgrāme bhīmadarśane
english: What Karṇa then accomplished in that battle, dreadful to behold, no other among all beings could have done, O bestower of honor.

sanskrit: sa hanyamāno nārācair dhārābhir iva parvataḥ gandharvanagarākāraḥ punar antaradhīyata
english: Struck by his iron shafts as a mountain by streams of rain, the rākṣasa—like a city of the gandharvas—vanished once again.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa vai mahāmāyo māyayā lāghavena ca astrāṇi tāni divyāni jaghāna ripusūdanaḥ
english: Thus that great wielder of illusion, slayer of foes, by his magic and his swiftness foiled those celestial weapons.

sanskrit: nihanyamāneṣv astreṣu māyayā tena rakṣasā asaṃbhrāntas tataḥ karṇas tad rakṣaḥ pratyayudhyata
english: Though his weapons were thus baffled by that rākṣasa's sorcery, Karṇa, undismayed, fought back against the demon.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahārāja bhaimasenir mahābalaḥ cakāra bahudhātmānaṃ bhīṣayāṇo narādhipān
english: Then, enraged, O great king, the mighty son of Bhīmasena multiplied himself into many forms, striking terror into the lords of men.

sanskrit: tato digbhyaḥ samāpetuḥ siṃhavyāghratarakṣavaḥ agnijihvāś ca bhujagā vihagāś cāpy ayomukhāḥ
english: Then from every quarter there came rushing lions, tigers, and hyenas, fire-tongued serpents, and birds with beaks of iron.

sanskrit: sa kīryamāṇo niśitaiḥ karṇacāpacyutaiḥ śaraiḥ nagarādrivanaprakhyas tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Strewn upon by the keen arrows loosed from Karṇa's bow, that one—seeming like a city, a mountain, a forest—vanished there once more.

sanskrit: rākṣasāś ca piśācāś ca yātudhānāḥ śalāvṛkāḥ te karṇaṃ bhakṣayiṣyantaḥ sarvataḥ samupādravan athainaṃ vāgbhir ugrābhis trāsayāṃ cakrire tadā
english: And rākṣasas and piśācas, fiends and ravening wolves, eager to devour Karṇa, rushed upon him from every side, and then sought to terrify him with savage cries.

sanskrit: udyatair bahubhir ghorair āyudhaiḥ śoṇitokṣitaiḥ teṣām anekair ekaikaṃ karṇo vivyādha cāśugaiḥ
english: With many dreadful weapons upraised and dripping with blood they came; yet Karṇa pierced each one of them with several swift shafts.

sanskrit: pratihatya tu tāṃ māyāṃ divyenāstreṇa rākṣasīm ājaghāna hayān asya śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Having beaten back that rākṣasa illusion with a celestial weapon, he struck down his foe's horses with smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: te bhagnā vikṛtāṅgāś ca chinnapṛṣṭhāś ca sāyakaiḥ vasudhām anvapadyanta paśyatas tasya rakṣasaḥ
english: Shattered, their bodies mangled and their backs cleft by his shafts, they sank to the earth before the very eyes of that rākṣasa.

sanskrit: sa bhagnamāyo haiḍimbaḥ karṇaṃ vaikartanaṃ tataḥ eṣa te vidadhe mṛtyum ity uktvāntaradhīyata
english: His illusion broken, the son of Hiḍimbā then said to Karṇa, son of Vikartana, "This one has ordained your death," and vanished away.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasmiṃs tathā vartamāne karṇarākṣasayor mṛdhe alāyudho rākṣasendro vīryavān abhyavartata
english: Saṃjaya said: While the combat between Karṇa and the rākṣasa was thus raging, Alāyudha, a valiant lord of the rākṣasas, advanced to the fray.

sanskrit: mahatyā senayā yuktaḥ suyodhanam upāgamat rākṣasānāṃ virūpāṇāṃ sahasraiḥ parivāritaḥ nānārūpadharair vīraiḥ pūrvavairam anusmaran
english: Attended by a great army, ringed about by thousands of misshapen rākṣasas—warriors who wore all manner of forms—he came to Suyodhana, brooding upon an old enmity.

sanskrit: tasya jñātir hi vikrānto brāhmaṇādo bako hataḥ kirmīraś ca mahātejā hiḍimbaś ca sakhā tathā
english: For his valiant kinsman Baka, devourer of brahmins, had been slain, and Kirmīra of great might, and likewise his friend Hiḍimba.

sanskrit: sa dīrghakālādhyuṣitaṃ pūrvavairam anusmaran vijñāyaitan niśāyuddhaṃ jighāṃsur bhīmam āhave
english: Recalling that old enmity, long harbored, and learning of this battle by night, he longed to slay Bhīma in the fight.

sanskrit: sa matta iva mātaṅgaḥ saṃkruddha iva coragaḥ duryodhanam idaṃ vākyam abravīd yuddhalālasaḥ
english: Like a rutting elephant, like an angry serpent, athirst for battle, he spoke these words to Duryodhana:

sanskrit: viditaṃ te mahārāja yathā bhīmena rākṣasāḥ hiḍimbabakakirmīrā nihatā mama bāndhavāḥ
english: "You know, great king, how by Bhīma the rākṣasas Hiḍimba, Baka, and Kirmīra—my kinsmen—were slain.

sanskrit: parāmarśaś ca kanyāyā hiḍimbāyāḥ kṛtaḥ purā kim anyad rākṣasān anyān asmāṃś ca paribhūya ha
english: And of old he laid violent hands upon the maiden Hiḍimbā—what need to say more?—setting at naught both other rākṣasas and ourselves.

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ sagaṇaṃ rājan savājirathakuñjaram haiḍimbaṃ ca sahāmātyaṃ hantum abhyāgataḥ svayam
english: To slay him with his band, O king, together with his horses, chariots, and elephants—and Hiḍimbā's son too, with his counselors—I have come hither myself.

sanskrit: adya kuntīsutān sarvān vāsudevapurogamān hatvā saṃbhakṣayiṣyāmi sarvair anucaraiḥ saha nivāraya balaṃ sarvaṃ vayaṃ yotsyāma pāṇḍavān
english: This day I shall slay all the sons of Kuntī, with Vāsudeva at their head, and devour them, together with all my followers. Hold back all your forces; we shall fight the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā hṛṣṭo duryodhanas tadā pratipūjyābravīd vākyaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: Hearing these words of his, Duryodhana was glad, and, surrounded by his brothers, he honored him and replied:

sanskrit: tvāṃ puraskṛtya sagaṇaṃ vayaṃ yotsyāmahe parān na hi vairāntamanasaḥ sthāsyanti mama sainikāḥ
english: "With you and your band at our head we shall fight our foes; for my soldiers, bent on ending the feud, will not hold back."

sanskrit: evam astv iti rājānam uktvā rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ abhyayāt tvarito bhīmaṃ sahitaḥ puruṣāśanaiḥ
english: "So be it," said that bull among rākṣasas to the king, and swiftly he advanced upon Bhīma, attended by his man-eaters.

sanskrit: dīpyamānena vapuṣā rathenādityavarcasā tādṛśenaiva rājendra yādṛśena ghaṭotkacaḥ
english: With blazing form, in a chariot bright as the sun, even such, O lord of kings, as the one in which Ghaṭotkaca rode.

sanskrit: tasyāpy atulanirghoṣo bahutoraṇacitritaḥ ṛkṣacarmāvanaddhāṅgo nalvamātro mahārathaḥ
english: His great car too was of matchless thunder, adorned with many arched gateways, its frame sheathed in bear-hides, vast as a measure of land.

sanskrit: tasyāpi turagāḥ śīghrā hastikāyāḥ kharasvanāḥ śataṃ yuktā mahākāyā māṃsaśoṇitabhojanāḥ
english: His steeds too were swift, huge-bodied as elephants, harsh-voiced—a hundred yoked, mighty of frame, feeders on flesh and blood.

sanskrit: tasyāpi rathanirghoṣo mahāmegharavopamaḥ tasyāpi sumahac cāpaṃ dṛḍhajyaṃ balavattaram
english: The din of his chariot too was like the roar of a great thundercloud; his bow too was vast, strong-stringed, and mightier still.

sanskrit: tasyāpy akṣasamā bāṇā rukmapuṅkhāḥ śilāśitāḥ so 'pi vīro mahābāhur yathaiva sa ghaṭotkacaḥ
english: His arrows too were like axle-shafts, gold-feathered, whetted on stone; and that mighty-armed hero was every bit the equal of Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: tasyāpi gomāyubaḍābhigupto; babhūva ketur jvalanārkatulyaḥ sa cāpi rūpeṇa ghaṭotkacasya; śrīmattamo vyākuladīpitāsyaḥ
english: His banner too, guarded by jackal and crow, blazed like fire or the sun; in form, too, more splendid even than Ghaṭotkaca's, its face wildly aglow.

sanskrit: dīptāṅgado dīptakirīṭamālī; baddhasraguṣṇīṣanibaddhakhaḍgaḥ gadī bhuśuṇḍī musalī halī ca; śarāsanī vāraṇatulyavarṣmā
english: With glittering armlets, garlanded with a blazing diadem, girt with a wreath and turban and a fastened sword, bearing mace and sling, club and plough, and bow—huge in stature as an elephant.

sanskrit: rathena tenānalavarcasā ca; vidrāvayan pāṇḍavavāhinīṃ tām rarāja saṃkhye parivartamāno; vidyunmālī megha ivāntarikṣe
english: In that chariot bright as fire, driving the Pāṇḍava host in rout, he shone as he wheeled through the battle, like a lightning-garlanded cloud in the sky.

sanskrit: te cāpi sarve pravarā narendrā; mahābalā varmiṇaś carmiṇaś ca harṣānvitā yuyudhus tatra rājan; samantataḥ pāṇḍavayodhavīrāḥ
english: And all those foremost lords of men, mighty, armored and shield-bearing, filled with joy, fought there on every side, O king—the heroic warriors of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tam āgatam abhiprekṣya bhīmakarmāṇam āhave harṣam āhārayāṃ cakruḥ kuravaḥ sarva eva te
english: Saṃjaya said: Beholding that doer of dreadful deeds arrived for the battle, all the Kurus alike gave way to joy.

sanskrit: tathaiva tava putrās te duryodhanapurogamāḥ aplavāḥ plavam āsādya tartukāmā ivārṇavam
english: And so too your sons, with Duryodhana at their head, were like men without a raft who, finding one, would cross the sea.

sanskrit: punarjātam ivātmānaṃ manvānāḥ pārthivās tadā alāyudhaṃ rākṣasendraṃ svāgatenābhyapūjayan
english: Reckoning themselves as it were born anew, the princes then welcomed Alāyudha, lord of the rākṣasas, and did him honor.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tv amānuṣe yuddhe vartamāne bhayāvahe karṇarākṣasayor naktaṃ dāruṇapratidarśane
english: While that more-than-mortal combat, fearsome to behold, raged on through the night between Karṇa and the rākṣasa, dreadful in its sight,

sanskrit: upapraikṣanta pāñcālāḥ smayamānāḥ sarājakāḥ tathaiva tāvakā rājan ghūrṇamānās tatas tataḥ
english: the Pāñcālas with their kings looked on, smiling; and your men too, O king, swayed this way and that.

sanskrit: cukruśur nedam astīti droṇadrauṇikṛpādayaḥ tat karma dṛṣṭvā saṃbhrāntā haiḍimbasya raṇājire
english: Droṇa, Droṇa's son, Kṛpa, and the rest cried out, "This cannot be!"—dismayed at beholding that feat of Hiḍimbā's son upon the field of battle.

sanskrit: sarvam āvignam abhavad dhāhābhūtam acetanam tava sainyaṃ mahārāja nirāśaṃ karṇajīvite
english: All grew agitated, given over to wailing and stunned out of their senses; your host, great king, despaired of Karṇa's life.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu saṃprekṣya karṇam ārtiṃ parāṃ gatam alāyudhaṃ rākṣasendram āhūyedam athābravīt
english: But Duryodhana, seeing Karṇa fallen into utmost distress, summoned Alāyudha, lord of the rākṣasas, and spoke to him thus:

sanskrit: eṣa vaikartanaḥ karṇo haiḍimbena samāgataḥ kurute karma sumahad yad asyaupayikaṃ mṛdhe
english: "This Karṇa, son of Vikartana, is locked with Hiḍimbā's son, and is performing a mighty feat, such as befits him in the fray.

sanskrit: paśyaitān pārthivāñ śūrān nihatān bhaimaseninā nānāśastrair abhihatān pādapān iva dantinā
english: Behold these valiant princes slain by the son of Bhīmasena, struck down by his many weapons like trees by a tusker.

sanskrit: tavaiṣa bhāgaḥ samare rājamadhye mayā kṛtaḥ tavaivānumate vīra taṃ vikramya nibarhaya
english: This share in the battle, here amid the kings, I have set apart for you. With your own consent, O hero, fall upon him in your might and destroy him.

sanskrit: purā vaikartanaṃ karṇam eṣa pāpo ghaṭotkacaḥ māyābalam upāśritya karśayaty arikarśanaḥ
english: That wicked Ghaṭotkaca, tormentor of foes, leaning upon the power of illusion, has long been wearing down Karṇa, son of Vikartana."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa rājñā tu rākṣasas tīvravikramaḥ tathety uktvā mahābāhur ghaṭotkacam upādravat
english: Thus addressed by the king, that rākṣasa of fierce prowess, mighty of arm, said "So be it," and rushed upon Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇaṃ samutsṛjya bhaimasenir api prabho pratyamitram upāyāntaṃ mardayām āsa mārgaṇaiḥ
english: Then the son of Bhīmasena too, O lord, left off from Karṇa and crushed with his shafts the foe that came against him.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ kruddhayo rākṣasendrayoḥ mattayor vāśitāhetor dvipayor iva kānane
english: Between those two enraged lords of the rākṣasas there arose a battle, as between two rutting elephants in the forest contending for a cow.

sanskrit: rakṣasā vipramuktas tu karṇo 'pi rathināṃ varaḥ abhyadravad bhīmasenaṃ rathenādityavarcasā
english: Freed of the rākṣasa, Karṇa too, foremost of chariot-warriors, charged upon Bhīmasena in his chariot bright as the sun.

sanskrit: tam āyāntam anādṛtya dṛṣṭvā grastaṃ ghaṭotkacam alāyudhena samare siṃheneva gavāṃ patim
english: Heedless of him as he came on, Bhīma saw Ghaṭotkaca beset in the battle by Alāyudha, as a bull might be by a lion.

sanskrit: rathenādityavapuṣā bhīmaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ kirañ śaraughān prayayāv alāyudharathaṃ prati
english: In his chariot shaped like the sun, Bhīma, foremost of strikers, scattering floods of arrows, advanced against Alāyudha's car.

sanskrit: tam āyāntam abhiprekṣya sa tadālāyudhaḥ prabho ghaṭotkacaṃ samutsṛjya bhīmasenaṃ samāhvayat
english: Seeing him approach, Alāyudha then, O lord, left off from Ghaṭotkaca and challenged Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmaḥ sahasābhyetya rākṣasāntakaraḥ prabho sagaṇaṃ rākṣasendraṃ taṃ śaravarṣair avākirat
english: Bhīma, the bringer of doom to rākṣasas, O lord, rushing suddenly upon him, overwhelmed that lord of the rākṣasas and his band with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: tathaivālāyudho rājañ śilādhautair ajihmagaiḥ abhyavarṣata kaunteyaṃ punaḥ punar ariṃdamaḥ
english: And so too Alāyudha, O king, that subduer of foes, rained again and again upon the son of Kuntī shafts whetted on stone and flying straight.

sanskrit: tathā te rākṣasāḥ sarve bhīmasenam upādravan nānāpraharaṇā bhīmās tvatsutānāṃ jayaiṣiṇaḥ
english: And all those rākṣasas, terrible, bearing weapons of every kind, rushed upon Bhīmasena, seeking victory for your sons.

sanskrit: sa tāḍyamāno balibhir bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ pañcabhiḥ pañcabhiḥ sarvāṃs tān avidhyac chitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Battered by those powerful foes, the mighty Bhīmasena pierced them each, with five sharp arrows apiece.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānā bhīmena rākṣasāḥ kharayonayaḥ vinedus tumulān nādān dudruvuś ca diśo daśa
english: Slain by Bhīma, those rākṣasas, born of the ass's womb, raised a tumult of howls and fled in all ten directions.

sanskrit: tāṃs trāsyamānān bhīmena dṛṣṭvā rakṣo mahābalam abhidudrāva vegena śaraiś cainam avākirat
english: Seeing them put to terror by Bhīma, the mighty rākṣasa rushed upon him with speed and overwhelmed him with arrows.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmasenaḥ samare tīkṣṇāgrair akṣiṇoc charaiḥ alāyudhas tu tān astān bhīmena viśikhān raṇe ciccheda kāṃś cit samare tvarayā kāṃś cid agrahīt
english: Bhīmasena wore him down in the battle with sharp-pointed shafts; but Alāyudha cut off some of those arrows loosed by Bhīma in the fray, and some he caught in his haste.

sanskrit: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasendraṃ bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ gadāṃ cikṣepa vegena vajrapātopamāṃ tadā
english: Beholding that lord of the rākṣasas, Bhīma of dreadful prowess then hurled with force his mace, like the fall of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ vegena gadāṃ jvālākulāṃ tataḥ gadayā tāḍayām āsa sā gadā bhīmam āvrajat
english: As that mace came hurtling on, wreathed in flame, the rākṣasa struck it with his own mace; and Bhīma's mace turned back upon him.

sanskrit: sa rākṣasendraṃ kaunteyaḥ śaravarṣair avākirat tān apy asyākaron moghān rākṣaso niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: The son of Kuntī overwhelmed the lord of the rākṣasas with showers of arrows; but those too the rākṣasa rendered vain with his keen shafts.

sanskrit: te cāpi rākṣasāḥ sarve sainikā bhīmarūpiṇaḥ śāsanād rākṣasendrasya nijaghnū rathakuñjarān
english: And all those rākṣasa soldiers of fearsome form, at the command of the lord of the rākṣasas, fell to slaughtering chariots and elephants.

sanskrit: pāñcālāḥ sṛñjayāś caiva vājinaḥ paramadvipāḥ na śāntiṃ lebhire tatra rakṣasair bhṛśapīḍitāḥ
english: The Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas, the horses and the great elephants, found no respite there, sorely afflicted by the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā mahāghoraṃ vartamānaṃ mahāhave abravīt puruṣaśreṣṭho dhanaṃjayam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Seeing that most terrible turn of the great battle, the best of men spoke these words to Dhanaṃjaya:
